title: UpdraftPlus Review
description: A local uploads backup checked in WordPress—not a full restore or disaster-recovery test.
metaDescription: A transparently scoped UpdraftPlus WordPress plugin profile from KreativWP.
highlights: The product is designed to back up WordPress files and databases
Restore capability should be part of the operational plan, not an afterthought
bestFor: Any WordPress site that lacks a tested, independent backup-and-restore routine.
researchScope: Started a local uploads-only backup and read back a known file from its ZIP. Documentation provides context for database backups, schedules, and remote storage, which were not tested.
caveats: A backup plugin is not a backup strategy until restores are tested. Keep at least one copy outside the production host.
thumbnailAlt: UpdraftPlus screenshot from its WordPress.org listing

handsOnTest.environment: Isolated local macOS PHP server; SQLite Database Integration; Chromium; free editions. Email sending disabled by a lab-only filter. No production accounts or site data.

checks.title: Create a local file backup
checks.detail: Started an uploads-only backup from the dashboard with database backup excluded. Ran due cron jobs in the isolated lab and verified the recorded uploads ZIP.

checks.title: Check archive contents
checks.detail: Read back the known fixture from the generated ZIP and matched its bytes to the original. The dashboard exposed the backup and restore controls.

limitations: This is an uploads-archive check, not a full plugin restore or disaster-recovery exercise.
Database backup, MySQL restores, scheduled timing, remote storage, and Premium features were not tested. SQLite is not a production MySQL test.
